term: "Grid Search"

## Simple explanation

Grid search tries every combination of selected hyperparameter values
and compares the resulting models using a validation procedure.

## Technical explanation

Given candidate sets for several hyperparameters, grid search evaluates
the Cartesian product of those sets. The number of trials grows
multiplicatively with the number of parameters and candidate values.
Cross-validation may be used for each combination, increasing compute
cost.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Grid search is easy to understand and provides a systematic baseline
for small search spaces. It becomes expensive quickly and can waste
trials on unimportant or poorly chosen values.

## How it works

Specify candidate values and an evaluation metric, train a model for
each combination, and select the best configuration according to
validation results. Keep final test data separate from this selection
process.

## Practical example

A classifier's regularization strength might be tested at three values
and its class-weight setting at two values. Grid search evaluates all
six combinations.

## Common misconceptions

- Grid search does not explore values outside the predefined grid.
- The best validation configuration may be overfit to the validation
  procedure.
- More trials do not guarantee a better deployed model.
